narrative.intro: New Hampshire has recorded $1.5B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. The federal government awarded 3,523 contracts in the state, with an average award size of $429K. Obligations fell 48.1% year over year. The Department of Defense is the largest buyer, obligating $1.3B in the current fiscal year to date. Contracting across the last six fiscal years shows variation: FY21 totaled $1.8B, FY22 totaled $1.7B, FY23 totaled $1.9B, FY24 totaled $2.9B, FY25 totaled $2.9B, and FY26 totaled $1.5B. Defense-related industries dominate the vendor and industry lists. BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. received $669M and SIG SAUER INC. received $286M in FY2026 to date. Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing is the largest NAICS category, receiving $286M. All figures are contract obligations and FY2026 totals are partial, fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: How does FY2026 to date spending compare with prior years?
sections.body: FY26 obligations are $1.5B, compared with $2.9B in FY25 and $2.9B in FY24. Obligations fell 48.1% year over year. Fiscal history shows FY21 at $1.8B, FY22 at $1.7B, and FY23 at $1.9B, indicating FY24 and FY25 were the peak years in the recent sequence. FY2026 totals are partial, fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: Which agencies and vendors dominate federal contracting in New Hampshire?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the top buyer, obligating $1.3B in FY2026 to date. BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. is the top vendor with $669M, followed by SIG SAUER INC. with $286M. Other notable buyers include the Department of Transportation with $49.4M and the Department of Veterans Affairs with $27.9M. Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing leads industries with $286M.

faq.q: How much federal contract money goes to New Hampshire?
faq.a: New Hampshire received $1.5B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The state has 3,523 awards so far with an average award size of $429K. Historical totals show FY25 at $2.9B and FY24 at $2.9B, with earlier years at $1.8B in FY21, $1.7B in FY22, and $1.9B in FY23.

faq.q: Which agencies award the most contracts in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The Department of Defense awards the most contracts in New Hampshire, obligating $1.3B in FY2026 to date. Other buying agencies in the top 10 include the Department of Transportation with $49.4M and the Department of Veterans Affairs with $27.9M.

faq.q: Who are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire?
faq.a: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. is the largest federal contractor in New Hampshire with $669M in obligations in FY2026 to date. SIG SAUER INC. is the second largest with $286M, followed by ENVISION TECHNOLOGY, LLC with $68.9M.
